clue.text: U.S. auntie to whom a man half warms in' Egypt

definitions.note: stands for one who held power in Egypt, the slave-soldier caste that ruled there

parts.note: Auntie Mame is the American aunt of Patrick Dennis's novel and the stage and film versions
Luke is a man's name, and lukewarm means only half warm

explanation.surface: An American aunt meets a man who only half takes to her while in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: The man, Luke, is pinned down by 'half warms': lukewarm is half warm. The definition is loose, pointing to the soldiers who ruled Egypt for centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mamelukes were a military caste of slave origin who ruled Egypt from the thirteenth to the sixteenth century.

clue.text: A herb to spoil the drink ?

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a joram (or jorum) is a large drinking bowl, or its contents

explanation.surface: A herb ruins the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: JORAM is an old spelling of jorum, a big bowl of punch or drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking.

parts.note: Ratty's friend in The Wind in the Willows is Mole, whose 'heights' are little mounds of earth

explanation.surface: The great achievements of a rat's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, Ratty's companion is Mole; the only heights a mole raises are mounds of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mounds of earth thrown up by a burrowing animal are the 'heights' a mole reaches.

clue.text: That's when I do, as a pagan worshipper

parts.words: That's when I do, as a pagan worshipper
parts.note: 'I do' followed by the word for 'afterwards' spells a worshipper of idols

explanation.surface: Someone says when they will act, as heathens do.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer after 'I do' and you get IDOLATER, a pagan worshipper; on its own it says when 'I do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something will be done at a subsequent time means it will be done afterwards.

clue.text: The denigrator is at the door

definitions.meaning: one who runs others down, a habitual critic
the hinged metal piece fixed to a front door for rapping on

explanation.surface: A critic is standing at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A carping critic and the metal rapper on a front door share one name.

definitions.meaning: a fish's: the skate is a flat ray-like sea fish, so 'one's' gives the possessive form
to look slippy is to hurry, as one does gliding fast on ice blades

explanation.surface: A fish is moving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of a flatfish's name and a verb for gliding swiftly on ice blades share one spelling.

parts.note: a gull whose name breaks into a call to rouse a cat: 'Kitty, wake'

explanation.surface: A frightening bird menacing someone's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarming' means rousing like an alarm clock: the bird's name splits as a call to one's pet cat to get up.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small cliff-nesting gull named for its call.

parts.note: well-worked cultivated soil, the prepared top layer of the land

explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is soil that has been tilled into a fine crumb, ready for sowing.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, moistens with a fine shower of droplets
small boughs with their leaves or flowers

explanation.surface: Rain-soaked boughs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb for showering with droplets and the noun for sprigs of foliage share one spelling.

clue.text: Was old, distraught, whom Lear called " Clotpoll "

definitions.note: Goneril's steward, the man King Lear insults as a blockhead

indicators.note: something distraught is in turmoil, so the letters of the phrase are thrown about

explanation.surface: An aged man, frantic, insulted by the old king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges WAS OLD. In King Lear, Lear calls Goneril's steward a clotpoll, a blockhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswald is the insolent steward to Goneril whom the king abuses in Shakespeare's tragedy.

definitions.meaning: one's kin, the people one is related to

explanation.surface: A question about family stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is both an account given and a kinsman, so the plural covers stories and family members.

clue.text: This door-keeper returned lit up again

definitions.note: the outer guard of a Masonic lodge

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for lit up again is read backwards

parts.note: relit means lit up again

explanation.surface: A doorman comes back and lights up another cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses RELIT. A Freemasons' lodge has an officer at its door called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freemasonry the officer who guards the lodge door against intruders carries this title.

parts.note: the land of gold in the Old Testament, from which Solomon's ships brought gold

explanation.definitionFit: Ophir is the region of fabulous gold riches named in the Books of Kings, a scriptural counterpart to the mythical golden city.

parts.note: Jack is the knave in a pack of cards, so his manner is that of a knave

explanation.surface: Exasperation at a man called Jack's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; in cards the jack is the knave, so the adverb describes how a knave behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting dishonestly like a rogue or card knave is behaving in a roguish manner.

parts.note: the heavens are full of stars, and a show whose cast is all famous names is described this way

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at the impressive line-up of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens' reads as an exclamation but also describes a sky that is nothing but stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast made entirely of celebrated performers is said to be composed of luminaries throughout.

parts.note: a felled bole is lumber, and an elephant's nose lifts things off: the two senses joined together

explanation.surface: A heavy jumbo jet lumbers into the air at take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jet; it is an elephant, whose nose lifts things. 'Lumbering' points to timber, and the answer couples a timber word with the elephant's organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The main woody stem of a tree, cut as lumber, shares its second word with an elephant's lifting nose.

parts.note: the drums are eardrums, and to silence them is to rob the ears of hearing

explanation.surface: An instruction to a percussionist to play quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drums' suggests percussion; they are eardrums, and making them unable to hear is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone unable to hear, overwhelming the eardrums with noise, is to render them without hearing.

clue.text: Presented with a cauliflower? How' distinguished!

definitions.text: Presented with a cauliflower? How' distinguished

parts.words: Presented with a cauliflower? How' distinguished
parts.note: a boxer given a cauliflower ear has an ear with a mark, and the word also means singled out

explanation.surface: Someone sarcastically admires a gift of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cauliflower' is a boxer's swollen ear; to be given one is to have an ear marked, and the word also means set aside or singled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means set apart for a purpose, originally said of livestock with a notched ear.

clue.text: What a suspender does for sitting

definitions.text: What a suspender does for sitting

parts.words: What a suspender does for sitting
parts.note: a person who suspends a sitting of a court or parliament puts it off to a later time

explanation.surface: How a stocking garter behaves when the wearer sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspender' suggests a garter; here it is one who suspends a 'sitting', a session of a court or assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a session is to suspend it until a later date.

clue.text: Doesn't 'come' round as 'the rousing hornblower does

definitions.text: Doesn't 'come' round as 'the rousing hornblower does

parts.words: Doesn't 'come' round as 'the rousing hornblower does
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Little Boy Blue is told to blow his horn but lies under the haystack sleeping

explanation.surface: Someone fails to wake, unlike a bugler sounding reveille.
explanation.walkthrough: The hornblower is Little Boy Blue of the nursery rhyme, found 'under the haystack, fast' in slumber instead of tending the sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Not coming round means remaining in slumber, the state of the boy in the rhyme.

parts.note: ... Meryll is Sergeant Meryll's daughter in The Yeomen of the Guard, and the name is the Greek moon goddess's

explanation.surface: A dreamy farmer's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yeoman is from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard; 'moony' points to the moon goddess of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is both a title of the moon goddess Artemis and the sergeant's daughter in the Savoy opera.

indicators.note: the king's name is placed in the middle of the word for bed

parts.note: taken as written
King Lear, Shakespeare's legendary ancient British king

explanation.surface: An aged monarch lying in bed with poor eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LEAR inside BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are watery and blurred see dimly, the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Heard' playing " Here comes the bride". by a delayed guest?

definitions.text: Heard' playing " Here comes the bride". by a delayed guest?

parts.words: Heard' playing " Here comes the bride". by a delayed guest
parts.note: a woodwind instrument heard at a wedding, whose name is said like a late guest's promise 'bus soon'

explanation.surface: A late wedding guest hears the bridal march being played.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument plays the wedding march; its name, said out, is what a guest held up on the way might say, 'bus soon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a deep-toned double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

parts.note: the opposite of flared trousers is a bell-shaped hat, a bell for the top

explanation.surface: A remark about flared trousers being out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Bell-bottoms are flared trousers; the opposite, a bell top, is the close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat whose French name means bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a women's close-fitting bell-shaped hat fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Ye gods, what lots of spilt drink!

definitions.text: Ye gods, what lots of spilt drink

parts.words: Ye gods, what lots of spilt drink
parts.note: drink poured out in honour of the gods is an offering

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a great deal of spilled liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye gods' reads as an oath; it also names whom the drink is poured out for.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine poured on the ground or an altar as an offering to a deity is the ancient ritual meant.

definitions.meaning: more tedious, someone more dull to listen to
a beetle or larva that drills into wood

explanation.surface: A dull bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the comparative of 'boring', more tedious, rather than the plain adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworm or similar beetle drills holes, and the same word is the comparative of dull and wearisome.

parts.note: a tall military cap with a peak at the front and often a plume

explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military headdress with a visor, a hat worn on top.

clue.text: A spell of warm weather in old England

definitions.text: A spell of warm weather in old England

parts.words: A spell of warm weather in old England
parts.note: the Middle English spelling of the warm season

explanation.surface: A heatwave in the England of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' is both a period of weather and a way of spelling: the medieval song 'Sumer is icumen in' spells the season this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteenth-century round 'Sumer is icumen in' shows the old English spelling of the warm season.

clue.text: Port officer gets his fur ruffled

definitions.note: a harbour town, here the capital of a Greek island

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: fur that is ruffled is disarranged, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A commander is annoyed, his feathers ruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' rearranges FUR to RFU, after CO. Corfu is the main town and port of the Greek island of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu town is the chief harbour of the Ionian island, a busy seaport.

clue.text: Author at odds with his public ?

definitions.text: Author at odds with his public ?

parts.words: Author at odds with his public
parts.note: one who makes a book offers odds on races to the betting public

explanation.surface: A writer in dispute with his readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' suggests a quarrel but means quoting betting odds; the 'author' makes a book of bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf accountant who takes bets is literally one who makes a book.

parts.note: Archimedes cried out on leaping from his bath having discovered the principle of displacement

explanation.surface: Someone finds a lost item on leaving the English city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English spa city; it is Archimedes's bathtub, and the cry is Greek for 'I have found it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation of discovery attributed to Archimedes translates as 'I have found it'.

indicators.note: disrupting the letters of the naval duties throws them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone barges in and upsets the Royal Navy's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to disrupt' rearranges the letters of RN DUTIES; R.N. is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in where not wanted is to enter uninvited.
